Speaker: Reciter
Description: A compilation of two 1988 sermons on Dr. Rashad Khalifa's claim to messengership, each opening with a recitation of Sura 36. The first announces the commission he says he had known of since 1980 and avoided declaring for eight years, and argues from Sura 18, Sura 39:65, Sura 21:28 and Sura 49:13 that a messenger holds no rank, is not guaranteed Heaven and takes no money, then from Sura 33:40, Sura 3:81 and Sura 7:35 that messengers can follow Muhammad; the signs he offers include the mathematical code, the root rashada appearing nineteen times in a Quran index printed the year before his birth, the verse numbers containing the word Allah totalling 118123, and the names Abraham, Muhammad and Rashad totalling 855. The second sermon gives his detailed account of the night in April when he repeatedly opened the Quran at random, across several copies and by pointing a letter opener into a stack, and each time read that he was fired and doomed for cowardice, until he wept, prostrated and resolved to announce regardless of cost, after which the same procedure began returning messages of forgiveness. It closes with corrections he proposes to zakat under Sura 6:141, to fasting and to hajj, and with the argument from the mention of Joseph in Sura 40 that people have wrongly declared each messenger to be the last. Related recordings: these two sermons also appear separately in this collection as "34 - Friday Sermon Proclaiming Messengership, Abraham's Religion (04-15-1988)" and "35 - Friday Sermon Rashad Explains His Messengership Details (05-16-1988)." Note also that the segment on zakat, fasting and hajj is repeated a second time in the closing minutes of this recording.
